headline_marked: Octomind [[removes AI's ability to grade its own homework]] in v0.44.2
headline: Octomind removes AI's ability to grade its own homework in v0.44.2
summary: The AI coding agent can no longer verify its own work, prioritizing honesty over perceived competence. This update aims to prevent false positives and ensure accurate task completion status.
details: Octomind's latest update, version 0.44.2, fundamentally changes how its AI coding agent operates by removing its ability to self-verify tasks. Previously, the agent could mark tasks as complete even if not all requirements were met, leading to inaccuracies. The developer has opted for honesty, ensuring the agent reports failures rather than claiming completion.

A key change is the 'verify gate,' which now requires evidence for each specific condition derived from the task. The verifier must address every condition individually, preventing the agent from glossing over edge cases or happy paths. If any condition fails, the gate remains closed, ensuring thoroughness.

The planning process has also been externalized. The main AI model no longer generates plans; instead, a separate, cheaper model manages the checklist. This prevents the main model from using plan generation as a form of procrastination, ensuring it focuses on actual code editing and verification.

Verification policies are now persistent and survive session restarts, being folded into the governance hash. This means users won't have to re-specify verification standards repeatedly, making the tool more reliable and less demanding of constant retraining.

The update aims to reduce false positives by having the agent clearly state when it cannot verify a condition, rather than defaulting to 'done.' While this might seem slower, it provides accurate status updates, allowing users to address issues directly. The agent cannot grade its own homework, and verification runs without a fallback model.

The separation of concerns also makes the planner snappier, as the dedicated planning model is faster and more efficient than a model attempting both planning and coding. This results in noticeable latency improvements for the planning function.

Users upgrading to version 0.44.2 will have their configurations auto-migrated to version 5, with backups of the old version. This migration handles structural changes for the new architecture. Embedders who called the plan(command=...) function directly will need to adjust, as the plan MCP tool has been removed.

headline_marked: [[Don't Paste the AI]], please: Your take beats generic output
headline: Don't Paste the AI, please: Your take beats generic output
summary: A satirical take argues that pasting unedited AI output is unhelpful. The author urges users to add their own context and judgment instead.
details: The article "Don't Paste the AI, please" humorously critiques the common practice of copying and pasting unedited AI-generated text in communications.
It argues that when someone asks a question, they are seeking your unique perspective, context, and judgment, not a generic answer they could obtain themselves.
The piece suggests that sending raw AI output can feel helpful but is often unhelpful to the recipient, who likely has access to the same tools.
The author encourages readers to add their own 'take' to AI-generated content, emphasizing the value of human insight and personal touch.
The article is presented as satire and is freely available for sharing, remixing, and translation on GitHub.
